# critic-adversarial-3 — wave-46-asks-nothing, the fix row T31

Reader: w46-T33, at head 6b7563afb608fccbdcf93beaff95655b086f2d77, in the main checkout. I wrote none of this code. The range holds e38e7518 (the entry's `### The reviews`, written by `bionic line`), T31's commit 900421bb and its landing merge 1df303f2, and 6b7563af (`line: release numbers T31`, author `bionic line <line@bionic.invalid>` by `git show -s --format='%an <%ae>' 6b7563afb`; the landing record's `ev=published|row=T31|…|numbers=6b7563afb608…` at landing-proofs.log:919 names it as the landing's own render).

The range opens at T30's head, 5a08f601. `git log --oneline --first-parent 5a08f601..31da41f7` prints one commit, 31da41f71 `merge wt/46-T19 (land)`, T19's release-set landing. Its branch carries four commits: d2e50621 (ADR-074), 1bb46ccd (the 1.29.0 entry, plugin.json 1.29.0, help and version rendered, the manifest refreshed), 69c0ce45 (the two §REL-1.28.0 arms retargeted to the 1.28.0 block and a pinned 1.28.0 manifest), and 91808ea8 (the entry's Known limits, committed by the line verb). `git diff --stat 5a08f601..31da41f7` names CHANGELOG.md, the ADR copy, plugin.json, help.md, version.md, rendered.sha256 and tests/release-check.test.sh. e38e7518, the reviews part the verb committed, comes after 31da41f7 and was already in my reading. The entry they wrote is the one adversarial finding 1 rests on, so they support that finding and change no verdict.

## Findings

1. **The release entry was not brought up to T31.** The 1.29.0 entry gives every landed row a bullet: T1 to T29 under the row list and the themed sections, and T17, T18, T19 and T30 under the walk, critic and release sections (`awk '/^## 1.29.0/{p=1} /^### The reviews/{p=0} p' CHANGELOG.md | grep -n '^- T[0-9]*'`). It has none for T31, and `grep -c 'T31\|matrix-render'` over that block prints 0. So 1.29.0 ships a changed `task:` rule in matrix-render that its release notes never mention. The entry also says nothing of the window. The 1.28.0 entry's Known limits carry "The hand-holds window starts at the newest build landing, so a fix row landing after the review moves the start past every act before it" (CHANGELOG.md, the 1.28.0 Known limits). T31 is such a fix row, and A-orch.44 records the effect: "The hand-holds line now reads total=0 · status-writes=0 (window since T31's landing)", after A-orch.37's `total=1 · status-writes=1` for the AC-4.1 task write. The person ruled this route (D19 "2", design-ledger Δ17, A-orch.42), so the ruling is not the finding; the entry meeting a listed limit without saying so is. The regression line (`CHANGELOG.md:141`, "three whole runs") is stale for the same reason: a fourth ran green at this head (`regression-run-6b7563afb608fccbdcf93beaff95655b086f2d77.log`, `Gating: 127 passed, 0 failed`, `rc=0`). T32, the doc row that would have re-rendered the entry, was dropped because the landing re-renders the numbers block (A-orch.44); that machinery writes only the numbers, so the prose was left. S3: release-note content is not a core function. User-facing on: a person reads the entry and the close's zero.
2. **Two arms, one fixture row.** taskof picks the one serving row of kind close (`hooks/session-poker.sh:3196`), else the one at step 9 (`:3197`, `:3202`). §CLOSE-TASK builds `ct_row T3 9 close REQ-1` and, for CT-4, `ct_row T6 9 close REQ-1` (`grep -n 'ct_row T' tests/session-poker-4.test.sh` prints lines 1887 and 1904). Every close row is a step-9 row and every step-9 row a close row. With the kind arm deleted, CT-1 still gets T3 through the step-9 arm and CT-4 still reads pending on two step-9 rows. With the step-9 arm deleted, CT-1 gets T3 through the kind arm. A kind read from the wrong field would also pass. The writer reports the step-9 fallback as unpinned (A-T31.3); the kind arm, the rule's primary path, has no row that tells it from the fallback either. Shown by reading the fixture and the arms; no mutant was run (my brief allows one suite and no other run). S4, a gap in test tooling. User-facing off: on the live plan T21 is both (`| T21 | 9 | close |`, plan line 114), so either arm alone gives the same answer there.
3. **Comments that lag the code.** `hooks/poker/plan.sh:620` says matrix-render's `task:` is "the one row serving it", `:624` gives `serves_load(spec)` as `<id><TAB><serves>`, and `:1848` says `task:` is "the one `## Tasks` row whose serves cell names the criterion or its requirement, else `pending`". Line 622 lists the globals the concatenated awk programs own (`nt tid[] serves[]` …), the contract that keeps LE_AWK and MR_AWK names apart; it now omits `tstep[]` and `tkind[]`. The writer reported all three as drift outside Files (T31-report.md, Concerns). The file is outside the reviewed range; the code it describes is inside it. S4, a comment that misstates the code; off.

## Questions the brief named

- **Close row only for the hand-holds criterion, every other several-row criterion pending?** Yes. `hooks/session-poker.sh:3200` returns `pending` when more than one row serves and `eev[cr] !~ /landing-report[ \t]+--hand-holds/`. CT-2 pins it: AC-1.2, served by the same three rows with eval `tests/b.test.sh`, reads pending. A mutant taking the close row for any criterion would turn CT-2 red. Falsification failed.
- **A second close row?** `if (nk) return (nk == 1) ? ik : "pending"` (`:3201`) never falls through to step 9 (A-T31.1). CT-4 renders a fresh copy with T6 added and reads `0|pending|T4`. Dropping the `nk == 1` test would return T6 and turn CT-4 red. Falsification failed.
- **The step-9 fallback has no row.** Finding 2, rated S4 off.
- **Is the red a red of the new row against the pre-change hook?** Yes. T31-session-poker-4-red.log opens `head=e38e7518e2f7f93a749071ea40e17eee009468ff dirty=1` with roots in the T31 tree, and its only failure is `FAIL: CT-1 … expected '0|T3', got '0|pending'` (line 536), then `500/501 passed, 1 failed` and `rc=1`. CT-2 to CT-4 pass there, as guards should. One record oddity: the run ledger line for that run, landing-proofs.log:910, reads `rc=0`, because the writer's command ended in `tail -3 "$LOG"` (`.bionic/tmp/runs/w46-T31-session-poker-4.test.sh.log.key`), so booked.sh saw the tail's exit. What that line feeds downstream is unverified; I raise no finding on it.
- **Did the comment compaction remove a pin?** No. `git diff 31da41f7..wave/46-asks-nothing -- tests/session-poker-4.test.sh | grep -E '^-' | grep -vE '^--- ' | grep -vE '^-[[:space:]]*#'` prints nothing: every removed line is a comment. My run of the suite at this head is green (below).
- **Does LE_AWK read the wider spec the same?** `serves_load` still takes `tv[1]` and `tv[2]` as before; the new fields only fill `tstep[]` and `tkind[]`, which `grep -n 'tstep\|tkind'` finds nowhere but session-poker.sh lines 3132, 3196 and 3197. The two callers of `serves_tasks` are `hooks/poker/line.sh:30` (LE_TASKS) and `hooks/poker/plan.sh:1867` (MR_TASKS). At the landing, the verdict logs read `landing-line-1.test.sh: 328/328 passed` and `landing-line-2.test.sh: 215/215 passed` (line/T31-landing-line-1-1df303f2f7aa.log, line/T31-landing-line-2-1df303f2f7aa.log; landing-proofs.log:917-918, `result=green`).
- **The plan.sh comments.** Finding 3, rated S4 off.

## Other attempts

- **A non-close criterion caught by the predicate.** A criterion that tests the measure on a fixture could name `landing-report --hand-holds` in its eval. If a close row also served it, it would now be owed at Step 9 and close-out would write it from the close's reading. `grep -n 'hand-holds'` over the plan's Eval design finds only AC-4.1's row (plan line 66), and matrix_close_rows already selects by the same predicate plus step 9, so T31 follows the design's own rule. Falsification failed for this wave; the general case is the duplicate the structure record carries.
- **Reach.** taskof runs inside MR_AWK, which `poker_verb_matrix_render` (`hooks/poker/plan.sh:1860`) runs on `session-poker.sh matrix-render`. CT-1 drives it through `poke "$RCT" matrix-render`. No new site is unreachable.
- **Trust and failure.** The only input is the plan's own Tasks and Eval design cells. No permission is exercised. Every unresolved case returns `pending`, the value before T31, so the change fails closed.
- **The live plan.** AC-4.1's block already reads `task: T21` (plan, `awk '/^AC-4.1:/{p=1} p'`), written by hand at 04:58:30Z (A-orch.30, A-orch.37). matrix-render never rewrites a present key, so T31 changes nothing on this plan; it serves the next run's Step 3.
